name: SaaS and developer tools
description: Subscription software, APIs, and technical products.

hasDefinedTerm.name: ARR
hasDefinedTerm.description: Contracted subscription revenue normalized to a yearly figure.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MRR
hasDefinedTerm.description: Contracted subscription revenue normalized to a monthly figure.

hasDefinedTerm.name: churn
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of customers or revenue lost in a period.

hasDefinedTerm.name: logo churn
hasDefinedTerm.description: Churn counted by number of customers rather than by revenue.

hasDefinedTerm.name: revenue churn
hasDefinedTerm.description: Churn counted by lost revenue. Can differ sharply from logo churn if losses skew large or small.

hasDefinedTerm.name: NRR
hasDefinedTerm.description: Revenue from existing customers this period versus last, including expansion and churn. Above 100% means growth without new logos.

hasDefinedTerm.name: GRR
hasDefinedTerm.description: Retention excluding expansion. Shows the true floor beneath a revenue base.

hasDefinedTerm.name: expansion revenue
hasDefinedTerm.description: Additional revenue from existing customers through upgrades, seats, or usage.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CAC payback
hasDefinedTerm.description: How long it takes gross margin from a customer to repay their acquisition cost.

hasDefinedTerm.name: magic number
hasDefinedTerm.description: A sales efficiency ratio comparing new ARR to the sales and marketing spend that produced it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: rule of 40
hasDefinedTerm.description: A heuristic that growth rate plus profit margin should exceed forty.

hasDefinedTerm.name: burn multiple
hasDefinedTerm.description: Net cash burned per unit of net new ARR. A capital efficiency measure.

hasDefinedTerm.name: PQL
hasDefinedTerm.description: Product qualified lead. A user whose product usage signals readiness to buy, as opposed to one who filled in a form.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MQL
hasDefinedTerm.description: Marketing qualified lead. A contact judged ready for sales follow-up based on marketing engagement.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SQL
hasDefinedTerm.description: A lead sales has accepted as worth pursuing.

hasDefinedTerm.name: product-led growth
hasDefinedTerm.description: Acquiring and expanding customers through the product itself rather than through a sales motion.

hasDefinedTerm.name: sales-led growth
hasDefinedTerm.description: Acquiring customers primarily through outbound and direct selling.

hasDefinedTerm.name: free trial
hasDefinedTerm.description: Time-limited full access used to demonstrate value before purchase.

hasDefinedTerm.name: freemium
hasDefinedTerm.description: A permanently free tier with paid upgrades, as distinct from a time-limited trial.

hasDefinedTerm.name: self-serve
hasDefinedTerm.description: A purchase path a customer completes without talking to sales.

hasDefinedTerm.name: activation
hasDefinedTerm.description: The point where a new user first reaches meaningful value. The metric that most predicts retention.

hasDefinedTerm.name: time to value
hasDefinedTerm.description: How long it takes a new user to reach that first meaningful outcome.

hasDefinedTerm.name: onboarding
hasDefinedTerm.description: The guided path from signup to first value.

hasDefinedTerm.name: aha moment
hasDefinedTerm.description: The specific action correlating most strongly with a user becoming retained.

hasDefinedTerm.name: seat expansion
hasDefinedTerm.description: Growth in revenue from adding users within an existing account.

hasDefinedTerm.name: API
hasDefinedTerm.description: A defined contract letting one system call another programmatically.

hasDefinedTerm.name: REST
hasDefinedTerm.description: An API style using standard HTTP verbs against resource URLs.

hasDefinedTerm.name: GraphQL
hasDefinedTerm.description: A query language letting a client request exactly the fields it needs in one round trip.

hasDefinedTerm.name: webhook
hasDefinedTerm.description: An outbound HTTP callback fired when an event occurs, so consumers do not have to poll.

hasDefinedTerm.name: rate limit
hasDefinedTerm.description: A cap on how many requests a client may make in a window.

hasDefinedTerm.name: idempotency
hasDefinedTerm.description: A property where repeating a request produces the same result. Essential for safe retries.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SDK
hasDefinedTerm.description: A language-specific library wrapping an API so developers do not hand-roll requests.

hasDefinedTerm.name: OAuth
hasDefinedTerm.description: A standard letting an application access an account without handling the password.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SSO
hasDefinedTerm.description: Single sign-on. Authenticating once against an identity provider to access multiple applications.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SCIM
hasDefinedTerm.description: A standard for automatically provisioning and deprovisioning user accounts.

hasDefinedTerm.name: multi-tenancy
hasDefinedTerm.description: One application instance serving many customers with their data isolated.

hasDefinedTerm.name: sandbox
hasDefinedTerm.description: An isolated environment for testing against an API without touching production data.

hasDefinedTerm.name: deprecation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Marking an API feature for removal, with a window for consumers to migrate.

hasDefinedTerm.name: versioning
hasDefinedTerm.description: Publishing distinct API versions so changes do not break existing integrations.

hasDefinedTerm.name: uptime SLA
hasDefinedTerm.description: A contractual availability commitment, usually with credits owed when it is missed.

hasDefinedTerm.name: latency
hasDefinedTerm.description: The delay between a request and its response.

hasDefinedTerm.name: developer experience
hasDefinedTerm.description: How easily a developer can adopt and succeed with a tool. A genuine differentiator in this category.

hasDefinedTerm.name: documentation site
hasDefinedTerm.description: The reference and guide content developers rely on. Often a product's highest-intent organic traffic.

hasDefinedTerm.name: changelog
hasDefinedTerm.description: A dated record of releases and changes.

hasDefinedTerm.name: usage-based pricing
hasDefinedTerm.description: Charging by consumption rather than a flat seat fee.

hasDefinedTerm.name: seat-based pricing
hasDefinedTerm.description: Charging per user, regardless of how much each uses.

hasDefinedTerm.name: feature gating
hasDefinedTerm.description: Restricting capabilities to particular plan tiers.

hasDefinedTerm.name: design partner
hasDefinedTerm.description: An early customer who shapes a product in exchange for access and influence.

hasDefinedTerm.name: integration marketplace
hasDefinedTerm.description: A directory of third-party connections, often a significant organic acquisition channel.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SOC 2
hasDefinedTerm.description: An audit report on security and availability controls. Frequently required in enterprise procurement.

hasDefinedTerm.name: penetration test
hasDefinedTerm.description: An authorized simulated attack used to find exploitable weaknesses.

hasDefinedTerm.name: data residency
hasDefinedTerm.description: A commitment about which jurisdictions customer data is stored in.

hasDefinedTerm.name: procurement
hasDefinedTerm.description: The buyer-side process of security review, legal review, and approval before a contract is signed.

hasDefinedTerm.name: land and expand
hasDefinedTerm.description: Winning a small initial deployment then growing it across an organization.
